decision: Retain all 12 active images: seven Story openers and five chapter openers. No generation or replacement needed.

images.title: Daniel and His Friends in Babylon
images.alt: Daniel and three companions share vegetables and water in a Babylonian courtyard.
images.review: Four young men request/eat pulse with water, with a supervising official. Natural brown complexions/curls, varied cloth colors and coherent bowl grips. Individual name assignments within the four remain uncertain; do not invent a new named face from this group.

images.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Dream of the Statue
images.alt: Daniel speaks to Nebuchadnezzar beside a dreamlike image of a towering statue.
images.review: Daniel interprets before the seated king; the statue is an imagined visualization of the dream, not a physical statue in the throne room. Gold head, silver upper body, bronze middle and dark lower legs remain visible; feet are partly obscured by impact debris. Hands, arms and foreground heads show no definite defect.

images.title: The Fiery Furnace
images.alt: Three men emerge unharmed from a brick furnace as the king watches.
images.review: Three clothed men emerge, with a fourth luminous figure behind and the king watching. Do not identify the fourth figure as Michael or Gabriel. Friends retain brown skin, dark natural curls and lean builds; precise one-to-one naming remains uncertain. Visible hands/limbs coherent; flames conceal feet.

images.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Humbling
images.alt: Nebuchadnezzar kneels in wet grass beneath a spreading tree at dawn.
images.review: The king lifts his gaze/hands after his understanding returns. This is the recovery moment, not a claim that normal nails/clothes depict the entire period of abasement. Crown-free graying curls, nose/profile, brown complexion and leaner build remain compatible with the throne portrait. Visible hands coherent; feet covered.

images.title: Belshazzar's Feast
images.alt: Gold and silver vessels stand beside a lit plaster wall at a palace feast.
images.review: Gold/silver vessels and a lit plaster wall set the feast. The scene does not attempt the supernatural writing or portray the whole banquet. No people, no wrongly young late-life Daniel; retain v2.

images.title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
images.alt: Daniel stands calmly among resting lions as daylight enters the stone enclosure.
images.review: Older Daniel looks toward the king at morning, surrounded by resting lions. Compatible strong nose/profile, brown complexion, gray natural curls/beard and lean build after the intervening reigns. Clasped hands and visible lion paws/limbs coherent; overlapping/hidden anatomy remains unverified. Distant king is Darius the Mede, not automatically the later Persian temple ruler.

images.title: Daniel's Visions
images.alt: Wind stirs deep blue sea waves beneath storm clouds.
images.review: Night sea stirred by wind illustrates the vision opening, without conflating chapter 8 ram/goat or inventing a new Daniel face. Retain v2; the rest of the vision is not compressed into this setting.

images.alt: Imagined scene: A quiet canal runs between reeds and clay banks near distant buildings.
images.review: Canal and distant palace setting near Susa; imagined landscape, not an exact city reconstruction. Full native scene inspected; natural light/materials, no people or animals.

images.alt: Imagined scene: An open scroll, a clay lamp and rough cloth rest on a low table.
images.review: Scroll, clay lamp and rough cloth evoke reading and sackcloth; blank marks make no source-text claim. Full native scene inspected; natural light/materials, no people or animals.

images.alt: Imagined scene: Blue river water flows past a stony bank and green reeds.
images.review: Open river bank setting; no new Cyrus, Daniel or linen-clothed figure portrait. Full native scene inspected; natural light/materials, no people or animals.

images.alt: Imagined scene: An earth ramp rises toward the walls of a distant hill town.
images.review: Earth ramp at a fortified town illustrates siege language; not an exact identified archaeological site. Full native scene inspected; natural light/materials, no people or animals.

images.alt: Imagined scene: A tied scroll rests beside a window beneath a starry night sky.
images.review: Tied scroll and night stars interpret sealing and star imagery; no asserted verified artifact. Full native scene inspected; natural light/materials, no people or animals.

limits: Group name assignments cannot be established from appearance alone.
Chapters 7–8 occur under Belshazzar before chapter 6 under Darius; chapter order is not an aging ladder.
Distant people and covered anatomy cannot be verified in detail.
These are imagined literary scenes, not historical evidence.
